statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of eight public/unauthenticated paths. Authenticated posting, purchasing, cancellation, account settings, and destructive actions were not covered because no test account or transaction authority was provided.

paths.description: Community landing/feed: primary discovery surface and global chrome.
Discussion index: representative forum/listing and search journey.
Workshop index: representative dense catalog/listing template.
Community Market: commercial listing and account-gated action surface.
Counter-Strike 2 hub: representative game detail/community template.
Sign-in: primary authentication form and empty-submit recovery.
Japanese locale: representative translated narrow-screen rendering.

findings.summary: The theme is hard-coded dark rather than adapting to the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: DOM computed styles report color-scheme: normal and the dark-emulated screenshot is materially identical to the default dark surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and express light/dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), retaining a coherent fallback.

findings.summary: Browse/filter and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion/modern-CSS probe found no view-transition CSS, and the sampled feed/filter navigation uses abrupt page/state replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add same-document and cross-document View Transitions to feed filters and same-origin template navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state or expose reading/feed position.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show static chrome on a very long 15,707px feed; CSS inspection found no scroll-state or animation-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky chrome with scroll-state container queries or a lightweight declarative progress/scrollability affordance where it aids orientation.

findings.summary: State changes provide weak continuity cues.
findings.evidence: Feed category/filter controls swap content without transition/highlight continuity; no View Transition or scroll-marker rules were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add active-state, directional transition, and focus/scroll restoration cues to filtering and drill-down navigation.

findings.summary: The cookie prompt obscures a large share of core content on every sampled template.
findings.evidence: On the 360x800 capture the fixed cookie panel covers roughly the lower third of the first viewport and overlaps feed cards; it also overlays every desktop archetype.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the prompt footprint, reserve non-overlapping space where possible, and keep equally prominent accept/reject controls with persistent settings access.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is custom div-based chrome rather than a semantic dialog/popover primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS evidence identifies .cookiepreferences_popup and .cookiepreferences_popup_content custom containers; no dialog/popover primitive is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic dialog when modality is required, or a non-modal popover/banner when it is not, with declarative dismiss behavior and correct focus semantics.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-wide rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container/container-type usage; reused cards, search panels, and navigation are adapted only by global responsive CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, search panels, and navigation modules while retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Most sampled interactive targets are smaller than the recommended touch target.
findings.evidence: At 360px, the active probe measured 95 of 100 visible links/controls below 44px in at least one dimension, including 15px-tall hub links and 18px search buttons. Keyboard focus was visible, but touch sizing was not adequate.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS px where feasible using padding/pseudo-elements, preserve spacing, and retain visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Invalid routes fail silently by redirecting to the homepage.
findings.evidence: Navigating to a deliberately invalid path ended at https://steamcommunity.com/ with no 404 explanation, preserved path, or recovery message.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 state with a clear explanation, search, links to major sections, and the correct HTTP status instead of silently redirecting.

findings.summary: Load performance is far outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 13.6s, FCP 8.3s, CLS 0.391, Speed Index 11.5s, and performance 0.33; the CDP trace corroborated LCP 12.7s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP path, reduce blocking styles/scripts and image bytes, reserve layout space, and validate under representative mobile/network conditions.

findings.summary: The mobile feed has severe cumulative layout shift.
findings.evidence: The layout observer recorded CLS 0.421, including a 0.403 shift, while 84 of 99 images lacked explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/media space with width/height or aspect-ratio, stabilize fonts, and prevent late consent/feed insertion from moving existing content.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is heavy and highly render-blocking.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 115 requests and 5.88MB transferred, with 15 parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets; images contributed 4.57MB. Confirmed stylesheets are linked from the document head.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate/split critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, prioritize only the LCP asset, and reduce initial image payload.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,111KiB unused JavaScript and 105KiB unused CSS; the HAR includes 28 scripts totaling about 996KB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by community surface, remove legacy/duplicate dependencies, and defer modules until the relevant interaction.

findings.summary: Core images, search fields, and links lack accessible names or labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt (92 nodes), label (2 controls), link-name (24 links), and select-name; the image probe found 95 of 99 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decorative images, explicit labels for search/select controls, and names for icon-only links.

findings.summary: Important text and search controls have insufficient contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 3.36:1 search-field text and 3.1:1 card link text against dark backgrounds, below WCAG AA for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text/token contrast to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and test interactive states across the dark palette.

findings.summary: Heading structure is missing or inconsistent on major templates.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no headings, Workshop has no h1-h3, and the app hub starts at h3; landmarks exist and sampled keyboard focus is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each page one descriptive h1, nest section headings in order, and preserve the existing landmark/focus behavior.

findings.summary: Production JavaScript logs repeated console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured repeated console.error messages: “Missing config element # application_config” from community/main.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize modules that require absent configuration; guard startup and remove repeated production errors.

findings.summary: Image sizing and asset markup are not robust.
findings.evidence: Although doctype/UTF-8 are valid, 84 of 99 images lacked width/height and 14 were oversized; this aligns with observed layout shift.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions and responsive source metadata for every content image, and avoid oversized raster UI assets.

findings.summary: Legacy runtime behavior blocks modern browser lifecycle features.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a deprecated unload listener in prototype-1.7.js, a known BFCache blocker pattern.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers, migrate lifecycle work to pagehide/visibilitychange where needed, and retire the legacy Prototype dependency.

findings.summary: Representative pages lack descriptive meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Direct DOM probes found no meta description on the homepage, discussions, workshop, market, app hub, or login; titles are present and unique on interior templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unique, concise meta descriptions matching visible content to each public page template.

findings.summary: Most dynamic community content is unavailable to non-JavaScript crawlers, and many links are not crawlable/named cleanly.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 10% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML; Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors with 30 nodes and link-name with 24.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or statically emit primary feed content and real href links, then hydrate enhancements; keep link text descriptive.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The homepage and representative templates expose no canonical link; /sitemap.xml redirects to the homepage rather than returning a sitemap, while robots.txt otherwise allows public sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical URLs per template and a valid sitemap index/URL set consistent with robots policy.

findings.summary: Rich community entities lack structured data.
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph metadata but zero JSON-LD blocks; game/app and market templates expose rich entities that could be described without changing visible content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org JSON-LD for organization, game/software application, discussions, and market entities where applicable, matching visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are below a safe baseline.
findings.evidence: The page is HTTPS, but the headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. The timezoneOffset cookie is not Secure, and sessionid is not HttpOnly; all three cookies report SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff and framing/referrer/permissions policies; harden cookie Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes according to cross-site requirements.

findings.summary: Authentication is password/QR-only and omits passkeys and autofill tokens.
findings.evidence: The login probe found no WebAuthn/passkey usage. Username/password fields have labels but empty autocomplete attributes. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in/registration with password fallback and add username/current-password autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response lacks HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and CSP; no frame-ancestors policy is available as a fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors, a strict Referrer-Policy, least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and evaluate Trusted Types/origin isolation for sensitive surfaces.

findings.summary: Primary feed content depends heavily on JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML includes only 10% of rendered content words. The crawler screenshot contains far less community content than the browser view, though the page is not an empty shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Render primary listings and navigation server-side as semantic HTML, then progressively enhance filters and live updates.

findings.summary: The app-like community surface has no install/offline foundation.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no web app manifest, and recon exposed no service-worker-backed offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: For this long-lived app-like surface, add a manifest and a small service worker that provides an honest offline shell/fallback without caching sensitive data.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling is misleading.
findings.evidence: A nonexistent route silently redirected to the normal homepage with no error, retry, explanation, or correct visible state.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve failure context, return the correct status, and offer explicit recovery actions instead of presenting a normal-success shell.

findings.summary: Empty sign-in submission gives no visible or announced error.
findings.evidence: After submitting the empty login form, focus moved to the username input but no role=alert or visible error message was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after submission, show concise field-level feedback, set aria-invalid, and announce an error summary through a live region.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields do not advertise browser autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The username and password inputs have empty autocomplete values despite representing established sign-in concepts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, retaining labels and password-manager compatibility.

findings.summary: The feed transfers an excessive and poorly optimized image payload.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 4.57MB of 5.88MB to 66 images; the image probe found 84 non-lazy below-fold images, 35 legacy-format images, 21 missing responsive sources, and a 1.07MB top image.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, negotiate AVIF/WebP, size responses to display needs, add responsive sources, and reserve intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Media/CDN delivery dominates initial resource use.
findings.evidence: 111 of 115 requests and 5.81MB are classified as third-party origins (mostly Steam CDNs/user content), with user images dominating bytes; these are operational CDNs rather than known trackers but still consume the initial budget.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a first-viewport media budget, defer offscreen user content, and avoid fetching YouTube thumbnails/media until relevant.
